question.title: 成人写作课的两条参与路径
question.overview: 原创迁移材料。用局部证据与全篇结构共同判断，不靠主题词重复直接拼段。

paragraphs.text: A public library offered an adult writing programme and advertised it as open to anyone interested in telling a story. Attendance declined after the first month, although most people who left still said that writing mattered to them. Librarian Leila Ortiz suspected that an invitation to join was not the same thing as a practical opportunity to participate.

Ortiz interviewed former participants instead of treating their absence as proof of weak motivation. Some could attend regularly but hesitated to read unfinished work aloud; others welcomed discussion but rarely left work before the evening session began. These accounts raised a question about the programme itself: why did one shared weekly meeting serve such different needs so poorly?

One reason was that the meeting tied several activities to a single place and time. Participants had to arrive with a draft, discuss it publicly and receive comments before leaving, even if only one of those steps was difficult for them. A timetable designed around the library's staffing convenience had quietly become a rule governing who could learn.

To loosen that rule, Ortiz separated preparing a draft from attending a discussion and offered two participation routes. People who preferred quiet preparation could leave written drafts for brief private feedback before joining a small workshop. The early drafts from this route were short and hesitant, but several writers revised them repeatedly once public performance was no longer the first hurdle.

A comparable pattern emerged among people using the other route, which allowed them to send spoken drafts and exchange comments outside the scheduled evening meeting. Their first recordings often sounded uncertain, yet later versions developed clearer sequences and more detail. Neither route removed the need for revision; each changed the conditions under which people could begin that work.

The library kept the two routes while retaining a common expectation that every story would be revised. Its lesson was not that open meetings were useless, but that a single visible form of participation could hide different obstacles. Ortiz planned to compare the quality of later drafts rather than rely on attendance alone, so convenience would not be mistaken for either motivation or learning.

links.explanation: C介绍退出却仍想写作的矛盾，F通过访谈区分两种障碍。Ortiz重复只是人物线索，关键是从怀疑动机解释转到调查证据。

evidence.text: C的attendance declined但writing mattered引出F调查absence不等于weak motivation。
programme与participants保持话题，并不单独决定顺序。

links.explanation: F问同一次会议为何不能服务不同需求，A解释把准备、公开讨论、反馈绑在同一时段。

evidence.text: one shared weekly meeting的问题对应A的single place and time。
不同困难被同一到场规则排除，回应F两类访谈结果。

links.explanation: A把排除机制概括为rule，E用that rule回指并提出拆开准备与讨论的办法，随后介绍两条路径。

evidence.text: that rule回指A的rule governing who could learn。
E的separated preparing ... attending针对A的tied several activities。

links.explanation: E介绍two routes并展开第一条，D以a comparable pattern及the other route承接第二条，既有对象回指也有平行结果。

evidence.text: the other route需要E已引入two participation routes和第一条的结果。
两段都呈现早期犹豫→多次修订后的进步，形成真正平行。

links.explanation: B综合两条路径与共同修订要求，限定结论并安排后续比较。尾段判断需结合两条路径均已展开，不能只靠lesson一词。

evidence.text: kept the two routes要求前文已分别展示结果。
not ... useless, but ... hide different obstacles防止把改进措施扩大为否定全部公开会议。

question.globalLogic: C现象→F区别障碍并提问→A解释共同规则→E方案及第一条路径→D平行的第二条→B限定结论。A→E→D提供连续对象链；F的问题不能放在解释之后；B的two routes综合要求两个实例已经展开。
question.themeTrap: F和D都出现犹豫，但F调查的是障碍，D报告的是第二条路径的结果。C与B都谈attendance，前者提出问题，后者警惕将到场率当学习效果；同词并不意味着相邻。
